bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Personal Trainer Salary in Australia

If you are a personal trainer or considering the profession, knowing how your **personal trainer salary** is calculated is essential for budgeting and comparing job offers. Pay rates for personal trainers are typically set by the **Fitness Industry Award 2020** (MA000094), which covers gym instructors, group fitness leaders, and personal trainers. This guide explains how to convert your hourly rate into annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, and what to expect for tax and super.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

Annual gross pay is calculated as:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**

For a full-time personal trainer working 38 ordinary hours per week, the formula becomes:

**Hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if your award rate is $35 per hour:

$35 × 38 × 52 = $69,160 per year

If you work part-time or casual, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The calculator on our [timesheet](/) uses this same method. We assume 38 hours per week unless you change it.

### Award Rates vs National Minimum Wage

The **National Minimum Wage** from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour (or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours). However, personal trainers are usually covered by the Fitness Industry Award, which sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Commission’s Modern Awards Pay Database contains the exact classification rates. From 1 July 2026, award wages increased by 4.75% as confirmed by the Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides.

For award/agreement-free employees (rare in this industry), the National Minimum Wage applies. But most personal trainers will fall under the award, with rates varying by experience and role (e.g., Level 1, Level 2, or higher).

### Casual Loading: 25% on Top

If you work as a casual personal trainer, you are entitled to a 25% loading on the base hourly rate. This compensates for not receiving paid leave. For example, if the base award rate is $30 per hour, the casual rate becomes $37.50 per hour.

On our [timesheet](/) you can tick the casual loading checkbox to add 25% automatically. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – let the tool add it for you.

### Fortnightly Pay: Weekly × 2

Many personal trainers are paid fortnightly. To estimate your gross fortnightly pay:

**Fortnightly gross = Hourly rate × hours per week × 2**

Using the $35/hour example:

$35 × 38 × 2 = $2,660 per fortnight

This is before tax and super. Your take-home pay will be lower after deductions.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Employers must pay **super guarantee** at 12% of your ordinary time earnings (from 1 July 2026). This is on top of your gross pay – it is not deducted from your hourly rate. For a $69,160 annual salary, the super contribution would be:

$69,160 × 12% = $8,299.20 per year

Super is only required up to the **maximum contribution base** of $270,830 per year. Most personal trainers will be well below this threshold. For more details, see our guide on [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus a **Medicare levy** of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds, as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed).

For a personal trainer earning $69,160 gross, the estimated tax would be approximately:

- $0 on first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($18,201–$45,000) = $4,020
- 30% on $24,160 ($45,001–$69,160) = $7,248
- Total tax ≈ $11,268
- Medicare levy (2% of $69,160) ≈ $1,383
- Total deductions ≈ $12,651
- **Take-home pay ≈ $56,509 per year** (or about $1,087 per week)

Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more precise estimate.

### Comparing with Average Earnings

The **Australian Bureau of Statistics** reports that full-time adult ordinary time earnings (May 2026) average $2,083.70 per week. For all employees (including part-time), the average is $1,579.20 per week. A personal trainer salary of $69,160 ($1,330 per week) is below the full-time average but may be competitive depending on experience and hours.

### Key Takeaways

- Your **personal trainer salary** depends on the award classification and whether you are casual.
- Use the formula: hourly rate × hours per week × 52 for annual gross.
- Casual loading is 25% on top – do not include it in your base rate.
- Super is 12% paid by the employer on top of your gross.
- Tax and Medicare reduce your take-home pay.
- Always check the latest [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman for your award.

For more detailed reference tables, visit our [reference tables](/data) page. If you need to convert a salary to hourly, see [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion).

### Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
